prompt: Simplify $\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}$ to a single trig function. Write your answer like "tan(theta)".
hint: This exact fraction has its own name — it is one of the two quotient identities.

hints.text: This exact fraction has its own name — it is one of the two quotient identities.
Sine over cosine is tangent; cosine over sine is cotangent.

explanation: So the expression is already a single function in disguise: it is $\tan\theta$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Check it with a triangle
steps: Opposite over adjacent is the definition of tangent.
